open_points.subject: A10 rule 7 request_digest construction
open_points.text: "The request an approval covers is described, before sending, by: the method; the full URL with its query ... every header sent on the wire ... The request_digest is the SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of that description."
open_points.question: What exact JSON structure (field names, nesting, list-vs-object choices) must be used for the "description" before canonicalization, so different implementations compute the same request_digest?
options: Define a fixed object schema (e.g., {method,url,headers:[...],body:{...}}) with exact key names and array shapes
Treat the phrase as descriptive only and allow any internal shape per implementation
open_points.default_guess: Use a fixed object with keys method,url,headers,body; headers as ordered array of {name,value_or_name_only}; body as either raw-bytes digest or multipart parts array.

open_points.subject: A09 rule 2 path placeholder parsing
open_points.text: "every {name} in the path takes the input port of that name"
open_points.question: What is the exact grammar for recognizing placeholders in paths (escaping, unmatched braces, repeated braces, literal braces), and which malformed forms are refused at proposal time versus send time?
options: Specify a strict placeholder grammar (e.g., /.../{port_name}/... only, no escaping) and refuse any malformed braces in proposal
Use a permissive parser that only replaces obvious {name} tokens and leaves other braces literal
open_points.default_guess: Use strict tokenization: literal segments plus {name} tokens only; any unmatched or malformed brace pattern is refused as not invocable.

open_points.subject: M23/A15 timestamps for non-executed NodeExecution records
open_points.text: "NodeExecution ... started_at, ended_at" together with "every skipped node and upstream_failed node writes exactly one NodeExecution"
open_points.question: For records where no execution actually runs (`skipped_by_guard`, `upstream_failed`, owner refusal), what values must `started_at` and `ended_at` take, and must they be equal?
options: Set both to the record-write time (equal timestamps)
Allow null started_at for non-executed records
Set started_at from node readiness time and ended_at at write time
open_points.default_guess: Set started_at and ended_at both to the same record-write timestamp for non-executed records.
